title: Achilles — The tale itself
summary: Achilles, the Iliad's greatest warrior, chose a short glorious life over long obscurity. This study tells the myth straight and complete.
body:
Achilles, the Iliad's greatest warrior, chose a short glorious life over long obscurity. His heel was his only vulnerability, giving us the 'Achilles heel.'

Every myth deserves to be heard as story first. Achilles unfolds with its own logic — characters acting from motives the myth takes for granted, events following one another with dreamlike necessity. To know Achilles is to be able to tell it. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Achilles is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

The story is the data. All interpretation comes after, and must answer to the tale as told. A third sub-question asks how Achilles was visualized — in vase painting, sculpture, or temple relief. Related entries in this archive: Raijin and Fujin and Perseus.
key_points: The full narrative of Achilles preserved.
